court_name: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT BOMBAY, CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
petitioner: Giri Textiles, through Proprietor Chandrayya R. Pasnuri
respondent: Anthony Nadar and Jainam Silk Mills
government_department_involved: Labour Court, Thane; Industrial Court, Thane

directives.text: Register and acknowledge the High Court's judgment (dismissing Writ Petition No. 15779 of 2025 and upholding lower court orders) in the Labour Court, Thane records.
Retrieve and present the file for Application (BIR) No. 1 of 2014 before the appropriate Labour Court, Thane bench for further proceedings.

Ensure the Labour Court, Thane, proceeds with Application (BIR) No. 1 of 2014 to decide it on its merits, without being influenced by prior observations, except for the concluded issue of maintainability under Section 42(4) of the Maharashtra Industrial Relations Act.
Establish a clear deadline of six months from the date of receipt of this High Court order for the Labour Court, Thane, to dispose of Application (BIR) No. 1 of 2014.
directives.deadline_text: within six months from the date of receipt of this order

directives.text: Implement internal monitoring and prioritization mechanisms within the Labour Court, Thane, to ensure expeditious scheduling and disposal of Application (BIR) No. 1 of 2014 within the stipulated six-month period.
directives.deadline_text: within six months from the date of receipt of this order

directives.text: Ensure official communication of this High Court judgment to all concerned parties (petitioner and respondents) and the Labour Court, Thane, for compliance and record-keeping.

raw_summary: The High Court dismissed a writ petition challenging concurrent orders of the Labour Court and Industrial Court. The petitioner (Giri Textiles) had objected to the maintainability of an application (BIR No. 1 of 2014) filed by the respondent workman (Anthony Nadar) on grounds of non-issuance of an 'approach notice' under Section 42(4) of the Maharashtra Industrial Relations Act within the prescribed period. The High Court upheld the lower courts' decision, ruling that the objection was hypertechnical given the disputed employer identity and lack of clear termination communication. The High Court directed the Labour Court, Thane, to proceed with Application (BIR) No. 1 of 2014 on its merits and dispose of it preferably within six months from the date of receipt of the High Court's order.
